messages:
incident-bot: PAGE FIRED — PagerDuty service=redwood-inference-prod, trigger=High error rate 5xx, routed to service_binding=platform-infra-oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC2469135780 :rotating_light:

jamal: wait what? that's targeting platform infra - inference-oncall should own this for the model-serving cluster. we don't monitor that metric.

maya: @jamal yep seeing it too. I got a notif from the health dashboard. Looks like the PD service binding changed in the last deploy?

pd-bot: Incident INC2469135780 created by alert-rule "inference:5xx-rate". Escalation policy: platform-infra-escalation. No acknowledgements.

linh: this is bad — we have customers in a live demo. can someone confirm impact? @sophia any support tickets?

sophia: Support: we have 3 reports from the EU region — demo requests failing with 502. Not many users but high-priority demo for a potential enterprise. Severity risk: medium->high if we can't restore in 15m.

maya: quick checks: metric spike on model pods: 5xx HTTP from grpc-proxy -> kv-cache timeout. Sequence length in payloads increased. But routing to platform infra means the people actually oncall for inference didn't get paged.

jamal: I can temporarily reassign the PD incident to inference-oncall. Doing manual reassign now.

jamal: /pd assign INC2469135780 to service=redwood-inference-serving (manual)

pd-bot: Assignment successful. Incident reassigned to "redwood-inference-serving" and notified rotation "inference-oncall".

linh: ack, I see the oncall (maya) got the page now. maya can you confirm?

maya: got it, ack'ing and jumping in. @alex can you help validate whether the routing rule used a stale service alias? I remember a config rename in the last infra rollout.

alex: checking audit logs on the PD config. Looks like yesterday's infra deploy added a "fallback-service: platform-infra" entry into the inference alert policy. Probably an unintended merge.

maya: ok plan: 1) suppress noisy follow-up alerts (silence non-critical thresholds) 2) triage root cause on model side (linh/jamal) 3) open PD config rollback/change and add a guardrail so alert policy doesn't accept fallback-service without owner tag 4) communicate to support + customer.

jamal: putting temp silence for that PD rule (30m) to stop page storm:

```
# pd-cli example
pd incidents silence --id INC2469135780 --duration 30m --reason "temp silence while rerouting to correct service"
```

pd-bot: Silence applied to related alerts for 30m by jamal.

linh: digging into logs. I can reproduce 502s locally when seq length > 8192 and a KV cache lookup times out. Looks like a downstream cache host in eu-west flapped ~02:14.

maya: workaround: enable local request retry and reduce concurrency on the proxy. I can flip a canary flag on two nodes. Doing that now and will monitor error rate.

linh: thanks — I'm hotfixing a short timeout bump for the KV client and a minor retry backoff. Pushing patch to canary.

maya: patched canary, error rate on those nodes dropped from 7% -> 1.2% within 90s. Rolling to the rest of the cluster in waves.

sophia: told the customers we're investigating and escalated to AE. Keeping them on a 15-min cadence.

alex: filed infra config revert PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/pd-config/pull/432 - will remove fallback-service and add required owner metadata. Also adding a CI check to prevent missing owner.

jamal: after we stabilize I'll create a follow-up to run a full pagerduty audit of service bindings and schedule mapping. This is a big risk if someone else changes policy without owner.

maya: handoff — I'm going to be on this for the next 20m then hand to @linh for long tail. jamal if you can own the PD change and postmortem?

jamal: ack, I'll own the PD change and the postmortem.

linh: ack, I'll take the operational follow-up once maya steps off.

pd-bot: Incident INC2469135780 acknowledged by maya.

maya: updating incident summary: short-term root cause: KV cache host flapping in eu-west causing increased downstream latency -> 502s. Contributing factor: PagerDuty routing misconfiguration assigned incident to platform infra instead of inference-serving.

alex: quick customer note drafted: "We experienced transient failures for inference requests in EU caused by a cache outage; we've mitigated and are rolling a fix. We're also correcting our alerting config to ensure the right oncall receives pages."

sophia: sending that to the affected accounts now.

maya: once stable let's ensure the oncall rotation and PD binding are reconciled. linking runbook entries: runbook/inference/incident.md and runbook/pagerduty/service-bindings.md

jamal: creating ticket: TICKET-4897 "PD binding drift: inference alerts routed to platform-infra" assigned to infra-config. ETA for config rollback + CI guard: 2 hours.

linh: error rate normalized cluster-wide to <0.5% after full roll. No further customer escalations.

maya: thanks everyone. Final steps: jamal to own postmortem, alex to merge PD config revert, linh to file code fix for KV client backoff, sophia to close customer comms after final status.

jamal: starting postmortem doc now and will ping for reviews. tagging for postmortem template: #postmortem.

pd-bot: Incident INC2469135780 resolved by maya. Resolution: temporary retries + timeout bump and PD config revert queued.

maya: resolved, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
